raw_response.rationale: Full text (18 pages) read in full. No inferential hypothesis tests, regression estimates with uncertainty, standard errors, confidence intervals, t/chi-square statistics, or p-values are reported anywhere in the paper. First, the core institutional/governance comparison between centralized metropolitan water provision by the parastatal Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB, N = 1) in Bangalore Metropolitan Center and fragmented municipal provision by 10 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs, N = 10) with KUWS&DB bulk supply in the Bangalore Metropolitan Region (Tables 3-5, PDF pp. 10-13) consists purely of descriptive secondary benchmarking indicators and unweighted arithmetic composite scores (Service Delivery Index: BWSSB = 59.12 vs. 10 ULBs = 21.31 to 52.36; Performance Index: BWSSB = 56.2 vs. 10 ULBs = 13.8 to 47.2), with no statistical test or uncertainty measure. Second, Table 6 (PDF p. 13; discussed p. 14) presents only descriptive 1-decimal-place sample Pearson correlation coefficients (r) across the 11 utilities among the eight MoUD utility service and operational/financial ratios (COV1, COV2, CON, AVI1, AVI2, UNW, OR, RC-Eff.) without any p-values, t-statistics, SEs, or CIs, and none of the eight correlated variables represents a rule-type legal, tenure, governance-structure, ownership, or tariff exposure (UNW, OR, and RC-Eff. are utility water-loss and financial cost-recovery/collection performance ratios). Third, Figure 1 (PDF p. 6) only displays an Excel linear trendline (y = 4.7355x + 1.0387, R2 = 0.4423) on decadal census population growth rates (1881-2011). Flagging quantitative_synthesis_eligible = TRUE is therefore overstated.
